subject.title: [Feature]: Webhook hook sessions should reuse existing session when sessionKey is consistent (multi-turn support)

question: Should hook-agent traffic get an explicit persistent-session opt-in, and what hook auth, agent allowlist, and session-key prefix boundaries must gate it before https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75918 can land?
rationale: The change controls whether external hook requests may re-enter durable agent context, so the permanent API and trust boundary need maintainer intent rather than a new automated issue-fix lane.

options.title: Land Explicit Persistent Mode
options.body: Accept sessionMode: "persistent" as an opt-in with isolated defaults, existing hook auth, prefix checks, docs, regression tests, and current-head proof.

options.title: Keep Hooks Isolated
options.body: Reject persistent hook-agent sessions for now and update docs/API wording so webhook callers do not expect multi-turn continuity.

options.title: Choose A Different API Shape
options.body: Pause the current PR and specify another compatibility-safe surface such as a narrower session target or trust-scoped binding API.

recommendation.title: Land Explicit Persistent Mode
recommendation.body: Accept sessionMode: "persistent" as an opt-in with isolated defaults, existing hook auth, prefix checks, docs, regression tests, and current-head proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter already framed the issue-level sessionMode direction and has the strongest review-history signal for the product/security boundary choice.
